title: mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-authentication.md
snippet:
**Important:**
We recommend you use service accounts instead of API (Application Programming Interface) keys to authenticate to the Atlas Administration API. API (Application Programming Interface) keys are a legacy authentication method.
To use the Atlas Administration API to manage your Atlas clusters, you must authenticate your API (Application Programming Interface) requests. The Atlas Administration API accepts the following authentication methods:
- Service account access tokens ([OAuth 2.0)](https://oauth.net/2/)
- API keys ([HTTP Digest Authentication)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digest_access_authentication)

Service accounts are the recommended method to manage authentication to the Atlas Administration API. Service accounts provide improved security over API (Application Programming Interface) keys by using the industry standard [OAuth 2.0](https://oauth.net/2/) protocol with the [Client Credentials flow.](https://www.oauth.com/oauth2-servers/access-tokens/client-credentials/)
A service account lets you manage permissions and create access tokens that authenticate API (Application Programming Interface) requests. Each service account has a client ID and a [rotatable secret](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/rotate-service-account-secrets.md#std-label-rotate-service-account-secrets) that function as a username and a password for creating access tokens. To learn how to construct an API (Application Programming Interface) request with an access token, see [Make an API (Application Programming Interface) Request.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access.md#std-label-example-api-request)
**Tip: Service Account Token Best Practices**
Consider the following best practices when using service account tokens:
- **Reuse tokens**: Service account access tokens have a 1 hour (3600 seconds) lifespan, during which you can reuse the token multiple times. Avoid creating new tokens for every request.
- **Generate new tokens when needed**: While you can't refresh an access token, you can [generate a new token](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/service-accounts/generate-oauth2-token.md#std-label-generate-oauth2-token-atlas) when your current token is close to expiry. This prevents service interruptions and allows you to maintain authorized service account access.
- **Revoke unnecessary tokens**: When you no longer need a token, [revoke the token's access](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/service-accounts/revoke-oauth2-token.md

title: Authentication | Atlas Admin API v2 documentation
snippet:
# Authentication
The API accepts 2 different authentication methods:
- [Digest auth (http)](https://mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/authentication#doc-authentication-digest-auth)
- [Service accounts (oauth2)](https://mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/authentication#doc-authentication-service-accounts)
## Digest auth (http)
Send a digest token in the `Authorization` HTTP header to authenticate with the API.
## Service accounts (oauth2)
Learn more about [Service Accounts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/service-accounts-overview).
| Flow type | clientCredentials |
|---|---|
| Token URL | [https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token](https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token) |

title: Atlas Admin API v2 documentation
snippet:
The Atlas Administration API supports OAuth2 Service Accounts and HTTP Digest-based API keys. Service accounts are the recommended authentication method and API keys are considered a legacy option.
To authenticate with a Service Account, first exchange its client ID and secret for an access token using the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow. Atlas provides a token endpoint at `POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token`, which returns a Bearer token that is reusable and valid for 1 hour (3600 seconds).
For example, to [return a list of your organizations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-listorgs) with [cURL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CURL), first generate an access token and then use that token to call the same Atlas Administration API endpoint shown in the current example:
```
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -fsS --request POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token \
--header "Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "${CLIENT_ID}:${CLIENT_SECRET}" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
--header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
--header "Accept: application/json" \
--data "grant_type=client_credentials" | jq -r '.access_token')
curl --header "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
--header "Accept: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json" \
-X GET "https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs?pretty=true"
```
